analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת כָּל אֵלֶּה refers to the animals Abram took. The next clause, וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם, describes him cutting them in two, with the birds excepted at the end of the verse.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular. The subject is Abram.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The phrase אֶת כָּל אֵלֶּה means “all of these.” אֵלֶּה points back to the animals just named, and כָּל includes the whole group in what Abram took.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before the plural demonstrative אֵלֶּה.

draft.change: Add the root בתר with its verb and the noun for a resulting piece. Correct the occurrence gloss from “cry for help” to “and he cut in two.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:10 describes Abram cutting the animals down the middle and laying the resulting halves opposite each other.

analysis.evidence: בַּתָּוֶךְ locates the cut in the middle. Abram then places each בִּתְרוֹ, “its half,” opposite its mate. The paired halves show what the verb did to the animals.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular. The doubled ת marks the Piel stem. Abram is the subject, and the following אֹתָם supplies the direct object.

draft.change: Add Gen 15:10 as evidence for the existing object-pronoun sense of אֵת.
draft.definition: The direct-object marker carries a suffix identifying whom or what the verb acts on.
draft.evidence: In Gen 15:10, אֹתָם supplies the object of וַיְבַתֵּר, “he divided them.”

analysis.evidence: וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם בַּתָּוֶךְ means “he divided them down the middle.” The suffix refers back to the animals Abram took. The final clause, וְאֶת הַצִפֹּר לֹא בָתָר, expressly excludes the birds from the cutting.
analysis.morphology: The direct-object marker takes the form אֹת־ before the third-person masculine plural suffix ־ָם.
analysis.sense: The suffix identifies the animals as the direct object of “he divided.”

draft.change: Assign the occurrence to the existing תָּוֶךְ in twk and clarify its Genesis 15:10 evidence under tavek-middle.
draft.definition: The middle of a thing, here the place through which it is cut into two pieces.
draft.evidence: In Gen.15.10, וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם בַּתָּוֶךְ describes the cut. The following clause places each resulting piece opposite its counterpart.

analysis.evidence: בַּתָּוֶךְ tells where Abram cut them in וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם, “he cut them apart.” He then laid each piece opposite its counterpart, confirming that the cut went through the middle.
analysis.morphology: בַּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article, whose presence is marked by the patah and the doubling of ת. תָּוֶךְ is a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: The physical middle of each animal, where Abram made the cut.

analysis.evidence: After Abram cuts the animals in two, בִּתְרוֹ identifies each piece as the object of וַיִּתֵּן, and לִקְרַאת רֵעֵהוּ specifies where he placed it, opposite its counterpart.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as subject.
analysis.sense: put or set something in a place

analysis.evidence: After Abram divides the animals, אִישׁ בִּתְרוֹ לִקְרַאת רֵעֵהוּ describes how he placed the pieces. אִישׁ singles out each piece in turn, and רֵעֵהוּ identifies its matching half opposite it.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used distributively.

analysis.evidence: Abram cuts the animals down the middle (וַיְבַתֵּר אֹתָם בַּתָּוֶךְ), then places each half opposite its mate (לִקְרַאת רֵעֵהוּ). בִּתְרוֹ names one of the resulting halves.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: After Abram cuts the animals in two, וַיִּתֵּן describes how he places the pieces. לִקְרַאת רֵעֵהוּ specifies the position of each half relative to its mate, with the two halves facing each other.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ prefixes the Qal infinitive construct קְרַאת. Together they function as a preposition governing רֵעֵהוּ.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת marks הַצִפֹּר as the object of לֹא בָתָר, “he did not cut the birds in two.” The definite singular gathers the turtledove and the young pigeon of verse 9 into one group.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a common noun of common gender in the singular absolute. The singular refers collectively to the birds.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶת הַצִפֹּר לֹא בָתָר, לֹא negates בָתָר, “he divided.” Abram divided the other animals but did not divide the birds.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֶת הַצִפֹּר לֹא בָתָר, the bird is the direct object and לֹא negates the verb. Abram cut the other animals down the middle and laid the halves opposite each other, but he left the bird whole.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with Abram as subject. The form has no prefix or suffix.
